title: Document parsing depth: PDF classification and Model Plane OCR routing, Office and e-book conversion, bounded parsing and a per-org parse cache
summary: Branch on PDF (content-type and %PDF magic) in the scrape/crawl pipeline: classify pages as text or scanned, extract text natively with the existing lopdf code, and route only pages that need OCR or layout to the Model Plane document-intelligence provider. Add parsers:[{type:pdf, mode: fast|auto|ocr, maxPages}], per-page markdown and optional layout blocks with bounding boxes, and reuse the same OCR path for raster image URLs. || Add a quarry-transform document module that detects DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, ODF, RTF, CSV and EPUB from bytes and converts them to markdown under zip-bomb and part-size budgets, branch to it by content-type in the scrape/crawl pipeline, and add a crawl option to follow and store linked office/PDF files as artifacts. Put resource governance around all document parsers (including the PDF path): a tokio semaphore, size ceilings, per-page time budgets, and a content-hash parse cache keyed per org and disabled under ZDR.
whyItMatters: Enterprise knowledge is mostly PDF; crawls that skip PDFs leave the Data Plane incomplete and answers ungrounded. The pieces exist in separate planes (native text extraction in Quarry, Azure prebuilt-layout in the Model Plane) but nothing connects them for a crawl. || Company sites link office documents and enterprise users expect them ingested into the Data Plane. Untrusted binary parsing without budgets is also an availability and security risk for Quarry workers, so the guardrails must ship with the parsers.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Sniff content-type and bytes; classify per page (text-layer coverage, image area) into text, scanned, image or mixed with a confidence and pagesNeedingOcr; if text-based with high confidence convert natively with heading ranking; otherwise send only the pages needing OCR to an OCR/layout service and merge per page; emit markdown, optional pages[] and blocks[{type,label,bbox,content}]; mode fast fails with a typed OCR_REQUIRED error on scans. Images: if the parsers list includes image and OCR is enabled, submit as a one-page document, else return a typed unsupported-file error. || Merged items add: Detect by magic bytes plus extension hint. DOCX: unzip with byte and per-part budgets (128 MB total), parse document.xml, _rels and header/footer with roxmltree to markdown; XLSX: sheets to GFM tables (calamine); PPTX: slide text in order; CSV to table; EPUB: XHTML chapters to markdown. A crawl option (saveFiles/contentTypes) stores matched binaries. Guardrails: key = sha256(bytes)(+variant); check cache; acquire a semaphore permit (default 3, FIFO); large files go by reference to an async job that a second request for the same hash adopts; time budget estimated per page; refresh bypasses the cache only within a small per-org budget.

title: Agent presence and run control UX: animated cursor and target highlight, real annotation markers, steer/queue follow-ups, needs-attention notifications
summary: Build one overlay layer in BrowserChrome that maps Quarry AX-ref rects (scaled to the frame) onto the frame stream. Use it for (a) an agent cursor and element highlight driven by the target rect that Quarry includes in the pre-action event, without blocking execution on a UI acknowledgement, and (b) an annotation mode where the user marks an element, text or region and the markers stay anchored to AX refs; a batch is sent to chat as one message carrying role, name, ref or selector, rect, nearby text, frame path and an optional screenshot. As an immediate small step, stop advertising the 'annotate' capability and remove the hard-coded placeholder anchor until this is real. || Include the target box/point in Quarry step 'started' events and render an animated cursor plus target highlight over the live frame in BrowserChrome (presentation-only, reduced-motion aware). Add steer and queue commands for browser runs with idempotency keys and expectedTurnId, consumed by execution-core at step boundaries, reusing Quarry's seq replay. Have Application Plane notification-core emit needs_approval, completed and failed notifications from run events.
whyItMatters: It makes agent actions legible and trustworthy during co-browsing, gives users a precise way to tell the agent what to change or extract, and removes a visibly fake feature: the gateway advertises annotate while the UI shows one fixed marker. || Users can follow and trust what the AI does in the shared browser, redirect it mid-run ('no, the second result') without restarting, and leave a run in the background until approval is needed. These are the daily-use expectations once the loop is live.

Annotation: comment payload {pageUrl, framePath, selectedText or targetDescription, targetRole, targetName, targetSelector, targetPath, targetRect, nearbyText, additionalSelections, marker point, screenshot}; overlay modes browse and comment; batch mode collects several comments before sending. Verevon: Quarry emits the target point from the AX-ref bbox before executing and may wait a short fixed delay instead of an ack. || Merged items add: Cursor: before each pointer action the executor emits {moveSequence, x, y}; the UI animates an overlay and acks. Steering: command {id (idempotency), type, expectedTurnId}; the server acks and emits events with monotonically increasing per-run seq; steer injects a user message at the next step boundary (optionally interrupting the in-flight step); queue appends to the run inbox. State changes publish notifications that the task list and approvals subscribe to.

title: Governed downloads and uploads: quarantined, tenant-scoped artifacts, a downloads drawer and hand-off to the Data Plane
summary: Turn on downloads in the Chromiumoxide driver: route downloads to a per-session quarantine directory and register the result as a tenant-scoped Quarry artifact (size and type limits, hash, malware-scan hook), withheld under ZDR. User-initiated downloads under takeover are allowed; agent downloads need the existing single-use sensitive download_ref child grant, and unsolicited downloads are cancelled. Emit started, in_progress, complete, failed and canceled events into the timeline, and add a downloads drawer in BrowserChrome with 'Save to Knowledge'. || Flip on the already-implemented artifact-only upload/download path in the Quarry driver (the capability flag is false today). Store downloads as Quarry artifacts with checksum, MIME sniffing and malware scan, and hand them to the Data Plane through its ingest API; allow uploads only from artifacts the run's owner can read, each behind a one-shot approval grant bound to the exact artifact and frame.
whyItMatters: Agents and users need to fetch PDFs and exports into Knowledge, and the authority model already exists in the contracts and the broker. Without it any page that serves a file is a dead end. || Agents that research or file paperwork need PDFs/CSVs and form uploads. Landing files as Verevon artifacts or documents (not on a desktop) matches the product's data model, and most of the mechanism already exists.

title: Parallel batch scrape with shared options, idempotent creation and wait-or-resume
summary: Make /v1/batch fan out under a concurrency bound (min of maxConcurrency, the org limit and the per-host AIMD scheduler) with shared scrapeOptions, appendToId, an invalid-URL report and the shared status/errors/cancel routes. Accept a client Idempotency-Key on crawl/batch/schedule creation (payload hash, response replay, 409 on key reuse with a different payload) and add a bounded wait_ms that returns a resumable 408 'processing_continues' response with Retry-After instead of failing or duplicating work.
whyItMatters: Sequential batches are a visible slowness for ingestion and for agents that want to read N search hits at once. Retries from the gateway or the Model Plane must not double-start crawls, and slow OCR/PDF/browser work should stop failing at gateway timeouts.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: batch scrape: 2 of 4 sources (Firecrawl, Codex declared only), common; sync-with-wait and resume: 2 of 4 (Apify, Firecrawl), common; idempotency: 1 of 4 and Firecrawl's is a negative example
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: POST /batch {urls[], scrapeOptions, maxConcurrency, appendToId?, webhook?} returns a job id and separately lists invalid URLs; status/errors/cancel reuse the crawl controllers. For waiting: key every heavy request by (org, request hash), wait up to the timeout, then return 408 {code:TIMEOUT, details:{state:'processing_continues', jobId, retryAfterSeconds}} with Retry-After so an identical retry re-attaches to the same job. For idempotency, copy the shape not Firecrawl's guard: store (org, route, key) -> {payloadHash, status, responseBody}, replay on match, 409 on mismatch, expire after 24 h.

title: Sitemap, robots and index-assisted crawl discovery, plus URL canonicalisation and redirect de-duplication
summary: Extract the /v1/map sitemap code into a shared Rust discovery module that also reads robots.txt Sitemap lines, gzip sitemaps, scoped, root and registrable-domain sitemaps, and URLs already in the local index or tracked sources. Call it from crawl kickoff behind a sitemap include|only|skip option, seeding the durable frontier through the scope filter. In the same enqueue path add a canonical_url unique_key and a post-redirect check so the same page is not crawled twice.
whyItMatters: Docs and product sites are Verevon's main knowledge sources; sitemap seeding makes crawls complete and cheap, and reusing the local index makes re-crawls incremental. Canonicalisation prevents duplicate documents reaching the Data Plane, which improves retrieval quality and cost.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (parallel sitemap kickoff, index seeding, URL permutation dedupe with redirect race handling)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Sitemap discovery: 2 of 4 sources, table-stakes; URL canonicalisation: 1 of 4, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Kickoff scrapes the start page then queues sitemap jobs for every candidate in parallel (3 concurrent, 25 nested max): robots Sitemap lines, <scope dir>/sitemap.xml, /sitemap.xml and the registrable-domain sitemap (plus /sitemap.txt). It parses urlset versus sitemapindex, decompresses .gz, recurses to a cap, filters each URL through the same scope filter and enqueues at a lower priority than seed links. Map is the union of index, sitemaps and optional site search, with redirects resolved, robots filtered and results ranked by query similarity. For dedupe, normalise (drop fragment but keep hash routes, optionally strip query, lowercase host); compute permutations (http/https x www x trailing slash x index.html) and lock the canonical one in a visited set before enqueue; after fetch lock the redirect target and abort if another job holds it. The limit counts the unique set.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Live crawl has no sitemap seeding. /v1/map reads /sitemap.xml plus up to 5 nested indexes and seed links, but not robots Sitemap lines, gzip or index-assisted discovery. Crawl dedupes on the exact link string only (visited map in workflows.go); there is no canonicalisation or redirect reconciliation.

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane. Move sitemap parsing into a shared quarry-runtime discovery module used by both map_routes.rs and crawl kickoff; add robots Sitemap lines, gzip, nested cap and URL cap with streaming into the frontier. Add canonical_url (unique_key) in quarry-core, a unique index on (queue/crawl id, unique_key) in the Postgres frontier, and a post-redirect check in run_page; keep aggressive normalisation (query stripping, index.html folding) opt-in per crawl. Seed from tracked sources and the local Tantivy index so repeat crawls only fetch new or changed URLs. Build after R-t2-05-01 so every sitemap URL passes the scope filter.
dependencies: unique_key column on the Postgres frontier
risks: Huge sitemaps; cap URLs and stream. Over-aggressive normalisation merges distinct pages on query-driven sites, so keep it opt-in.

title: Agent web toolset: content-hydrated search, next-step hints, citations, and Quarry jobs as approval-gated tools with cost estimates
summary: Let /v1/search accept scrapeOptions (bounded top-N, total time budget, shared fan-out) and give the Model Plane web_search tool a with_content flag so one call returns search hits plus page content. Add opt-in hints[] to success responses of scrape/search/map, computed only from local signals (truncated, empty, blocked, SERP URL), extending the existing next_actions field. Add a Model Plane tool-doc registry with a server-side 'docs read' check before high-risk browser tools, and attach stable source ids to tool output so answers cite them, with an org domain allow/deny policy honoured on service-token fetches. || Register Quarry crawl, map, batch-extract, pack runs and promoted procedures as capabilities in capability-core and as Model Plane tools, with parameter schemas taken from the pack schemas. The approval card shows an estimated cost and page cap before anything runs, and new service-principal scopes gate each route. A later phase exposes the same registry through mcp-bridge as an off-by-default, org-gated MCP facade with output-token caps.
whyItMatters: Agents get N pages in one call instead of search plus N fetches, waste fewer turns on blind retries, and use risky browser tools more safely. Org admins can restrict which domains agents fetch and answers stay traceable to sources. || 'AI proposes, Quarry executes' is only real if the Model can propose more than two web tools. Today the chat agent can search and fetch one URL, but crawl, extract-with-schema, packs and procedures are not agent-reachable, so the Model falls back to repeated single fetches.

title: Memory pollution guard for runs that ingested web or browser content (verify first)

title: Complete web-usage metering: browser metrics, outcome and surface attributes, price table and plan keys
summary: Phase A: add distinct usage metrics for browser steps and minutes, agent runs and extract/map (today extract and map are billed as search queries) with attributes {outcome, driver, llm_format, paid_provider, zdr, surface}, and a closed x-verevon-surface enum set by the gateway and Model Plane. Phase B: surface per-run usage in the ingestion run view. Phase C: add plan keys (browser agent loop, persistent profiles, concurrent sessions, schedules) in org-core entitlements delivered as claims, per-class rate limits layered on the gateway's global bucket, and a per-org fair-share concurrency cap in Quarry.
whyItMatters: Browser agent steps and minutes are not metered at all, so the most expensive Quarry feature is invisible to billing, and one org can consume every browser lease. Cost transparency for web acquisition (separate from model cost) and abuse protection are table-stakes that two or three of the four references have.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (single pricing function, failures free, two clear limit units)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Firecrawl: one pure function price(options, outcome, cost tracking, flags) per job: base unit per page, failures cost 0, surcharges for LLM or security features, PDF per page, a ZDR surcharge, with a separate tracker of real provider costs for margin. Two limit units (pages or credits, and concurrent browsers) with separate submission and status rate limits. Aside gates features per plan (for example remote control on pro and max only). Apify meters compute units (GB-RAM-hours) plus storage operations. Every Firecrawl request also carries an origin and an integration tag from a closed list for analytics and cost attribution.

Pricing lives in Lago billable-metric configuration outside this repo (INF, from the usage.rs comment), not in a pure function the Model Plane can call for estimates. org-core default entitlements are chat, api_keys, audit_logs and sso, quotas are api_calls, users and storage_mb per plan, and ZDR is the only computed plan-gated entitlement; no browser or Quarry keys exist. The gateway has a global distributed per-org/user token bucket (600 RPM default) over every route, but no per-class limits, and Quarry's browser pool is two or four process-wide leases with no per-org fairness. The SPA usage client is unused code.

Frontend gateway: add cheap/expensive rate-limit classes on top of rate_limit.rs; Frontend: per-run usage in the ingestion run view. title: Fetch-path reliability: one deadline budget, wired retries and typed failure sub-codes
summary: Add timeout_ms to scrape and agent requests and split it across the FallbackDriver waterfall with child cancellation tokens (reserve a minimum slice for the final browser tier, map client disconnect to the root token). Wire the already-written execute_with_retry into PageRunner using ErrorCode::retryable(), with maxRetries on the policy and no retries for ChallengeDetected or SecurityBlocked. Add a sub-code and detail field on QuarryError (DNS, TLS, all drivers failed, robots-blocked, and a processing-continues detail for long jobs), versioned across Temporal, webhooks and the gateway.
whyItMatters: Escalation through the static, TLS and browser drivers should finish inside one user-visible deadline instead of timing out with nothing. Transient failures should be retried the same way on scrape, crawl and agent paths. The Model and UI need to know why a fetch failed so they can switch source, wait or ask the user, instead of seeing a generic DriverFailed.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (SRC) for abort tiers and the transportable error vocabulary; Apify Crawlee (DOC) for the retry contract
others: Apify Crawlee (DOC): maxRequestRetries, errorHandler before each retry, failedRequestHandler
Firecrawl robustFetch (SRC): shared internal client with retry-on-status and cooldown
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Retries: 2 of 4 sources (Apify, Firecrawl), table-stakes. Deadline budgeting and transportable error codes: 1 of 4 (Firecrawl), unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Compose cancellation tokens: request token (client disconnect) to scrape deadline token to per-engine child tokens, so an engine timeout cancels only that engine and the waterfall continues, while a scrape timeout cancels everything. Queue waits get a fraction of the budget (2/3), waitFor is at most half the timeout, and defaults are computed from the requested features. One ErrorCode union with about 55 codes extends a transportable base with serialize/deserialize so code and details cross queues and webhooks unchanged; long jobs return a processing_continues detail with estimated remaining time. Retry: count per request, an error hook may change the request, then requeue with backoff until the retry cap, then a failure hook.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: execute_with_retry is exported but called only from its own tests; Temporal activity retries (5 attempts, exponential) and the FallbackDriver chain are the only live retry paths. Per the baseline, cancellation is a flat token, /v1/scrape exposes no request timeout and the waterfall has no per-driver budget (not re-checked here). quarry-core ErrorCode has 17 coarse codes with retryable() and http_status(); it has no fetch-level detail (DNS, TLS, all drivers failed, robots-blocked, cache miss) and no processing-continues contract, although api_error carries retry_after_seconds. Strict TLS everywhere is already the safe default (no accept-invalid-certs found).

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane. (a) Deadlines: add timeout_ms to scrape and agent-run requests with defaults computed in one function from the requested features; build a child CancellationToken per driver attempt with remaining-budget accounting in FallbackDriver and a reserved minimum slice for the last driver; map axum client disconnect to the root token; keep strict TLS. (b) Retries: call execute_with_retry from PageRunner, take the cap from RunPolicy.retry (exists in the quarry-core contract), skip ChallengeDetected, SecurityBlocked and robots denials, and consult the AIMD host scheduler so retries cannot storm a blocked host. Share one reqwest retry middleware for edge-to-control and Model Plane calls. (c) Errors: add a sub_code plus details to QuarryError (for example DriverFailed{dns|tls|connect|all_drivers_failed}, Forbidden{robots|policy}) rather than exploding the top-level enum, as the improvements doc section 39 also advises; add a processing_continues detail for long jobs; propagate through Temporal activities, webhooks, the gateway's recoverable/unrecoverable classification and Model Plane tool results; version the error schema.

planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (quarry-runtime, quarry-core, orchestrator); Frontend Plane gateway for classification
risks: Budget splitting can starve the browser tier, hence the reserved slice. Retry storms against blocked hosts. Contract churn for gateway and Model Plane clients, hence a versioned schema.

title: Org-scoped URL cache with explicit freshness, and a cache-only no-egress mode
summary: Add a URL plus variant keyed cache in Ingestion Plane over the existing artifact storage (Postgres metadata, Redis hot path), keyed by org, with maxAge/minAge/store flags on scrape and agent fetches, cacheState and cachedAt in the output metadata, and negative caching. ZDR orgs bypass it entirely. In a second phase add a no_egress policy flag that pins the driver plan to cache and Data Plane artifacts and returns a typed miss without logging the URL.
whyItMatters: Repeated agent research becomes cheaper and faster, fewer requests hit target sites (which also reduces blocks), and the Model gets explicit freshness it can reason about. The no-egress mode gives regulated or sovereign workspaces a hard guarantee of no outbound traffic.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique, with lockdown as a further unique mode
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Key = hash(normalised URL) plus variant (mobile, country, stealth, blockAds, wait, screenshot options). Raw body goes to object storage, a metadata row to an index table, hot entries to a Redis LRU that fails fast. The read path resolves maxAge (explicit, then dynamic per domain via a 200 ms race, then a 2-day default), queries the newest entry in the window and returns cacheState hit/miss plus cachedAt; negative windows skip the DB on repeat misses and entries whose body is missing are deleted. Lockdown rewrites the engine plan to index-only, disables robots/sitemap/redirect fetching, forces ZDR and returns a typed cache-miss error that does not log the URL.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: The Quarry cache is keyed by content fingerprint and is read only when the caller sends prev_fingerprint (and never under ZDR), so there is no URL or maxAge cache, no cacheState metadata, no negative caching and no cache-only mode; SWR claimed in PRESETS.md is absent. The gateway has separate 4 h search and scrape-preview caches (see R-t2-04-02). Artifact storage and Data Plane document storage already exist as bodies to serve from.

approachOriginal: Ingestion Plane: after R-t2-04-02 lands the shared should_cache(), build the URL index with org-scoped keys, store bodies in the existing artifact store, hot path in Redis, flags maxAge/minAge/store on scrape and agent observation fetches, cacheState and cachedAt in NormalizedOutput, negative cache for failures, self-healing when a body is missing. Never cache credentialed, action or profile requests, or anything produced under ZDR. Phase 2: no_egress policy flag (carried by the org policy floor, R-t2-04-05) that pins DriverPlan to a cache/Data-Plane-artifact driver, calling Data Plane APIs rather than its database, and returns a typed miss error without logging the URL.

risks: Cross-tenant leakage if keys are not org-scoped or authenticated content is cached; stale answers surprise users, so always show cachedAt. Lockdown value is limited to a niche of regulated orgs.
